title: Reconstructed red-cell dispersion modestly improves additive inflammation prediction, but not nonlinear baselines, from NHANES III to 2017–2018
abstract: A red-cell volume dispersion proxy, RDW×MCV/100, was evaluated for concurrent CRP >3 mg/L using 14,501 NHANES III adults for training and 4,603 independently recruited NHANES 2017–2018 adults for confirmation. Against a survey-weighted additive logistic model containing demographic, adiposity and blood-count measures including RDW and MCV, the weighted Brier difference was -0.00065146 (approximate fixed-fit target-PSU bootstrap 95% interval -0.00124576 to -0.00008550); AUC increased 0.001031. However, adding the same feature to a prespecified squared-main-effect comparator changed Brier by +0.00013758, and joint training/target uncertainty included zero for the additive comparison. A post-result additive-spline challenge likewise showed no gain. Thus the transferable additive-model improvement is small and model-dependent, not evidence for a robust new biomarker or clinical utility.
